Lemma
[short geodesics on a normal ball]

Source: petersen:page-0207 ↗ lem:pet-ch5-radial-geodesic-segment ↗ lem:pet-ch5-radial-geodesic-unique-piecewise ↗ cor:pet-ch5-metric-ball-image ↗ def:pet-ch5-segment

1. ch5:5.5.4bFor every $p\in M$ there is $\varepsilon >0$ such that

  1. $\{ v:|v|_g<\varepsilon \} \subset \mathcal O_p$;

  2. $\exp _p(\{ v:|v|_g<\delta \} )=B(p,\delta )$ for every $0<\delta \le \varepsilon $;

  3. for every $v$ with $|v|_g<\varepsilon $, the curve $t\mapsto \exp _p(tv)$, $t\in [0,1]$, is a segment, and every segment $\sigma :[0,1]\to M$ from $p$ to $\exp _p(v)$ satisfies $\sigma (t)=\exp _p(tv)$ for all $t\in [0,1]$.

This is subsection 5.2 verbatim except that $\varepsilon $ is furnished rather than hypothesised. Every radius is measured in the intrinsic $|\cdot |_g$, so clauses (ii) and (iii) agree on what the ball is. Clause (iii) is in fact stronger than the book's: it quantifies over every segment competitor — not only those declared to have speed $|v|$, since a segment's speed is forced to be $|v|_g$ by subsection 5.2 — and concludes pointwise equality with the radial geodesic rather than equality up to reparametrization.
Proof

↗ lem:pet-ch5-radial-geodesic-unique-piecewise ↗ lem:pet-ch5-radial-geodesic-segment ↗ cor:pet-ch5-metric-ball-image \sketch Choose $\varepsilon $ below the radii in item 3, subsection 5.2, and subsection 5.2, using norm coercivity to pass from intrinsic to model radii. For a segment $\sigma $ to $\exp _pv$, proportional arclength gives $L(\sigma )|_0^t=t|v|_g$, while uniqueness gives $L(\sigma )|_0^t=s(t)|v|_g$. If $v\ne 0$, cancellation yields $s=t$; for $v=0$ both curves are constant.

□
